name: Commitment schemes

subjectOf.text: SPoS binds validator votes irrevocably by requiring commitment via hash preimages that are revealed only after a designated period, driving the probability of successful post-facto vote alteration below 2^-128.
subjectOf.abstract: These schemes require validators to commit to votes via hash preimages, revealed only after a designated period, rendering post-facto alterations computationally infeasible with a probability of success below 2^-128
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Cryptographic Foundations and Interdisciplinary Dimensions of the Secure Proof of Stake (SPoS) Conse (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5225296
scope_conditions: asynchronous and partially synchronous network conditions

subjectOf.text: The seal is a commitment made visible rather than a lock, because the operator can open the files.
subjectOf.abstract: Intelligence models increasingly learn from data that earlier Intelligence models produced, and when that loop repeats the rare cases disappear first. This paper preregisters a test of whether a reputation-weighted validator pool, filtering the training data of a recursive replacement loop, keeps those rare cases alive. The outcomes remain sealed until a replication of the original model-collapse result succeeds.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Can Reputation Prevent Model Collapse? A Preregistered Test of Reputation-Weighted Data Filtering (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=7598518
scope_conditions: Concerns the sealed outcome store of Section VI.
The limit is stated by the paper, not inferred from the architecture.
